name: Tenant or Operator Boundary Unresolved
trigger_conditions: tenant or operator may control dominant loads
anti_triggers: single actor clearly controls and captures the dominant variable
lease and metering boundary fully aligned
physical_basis: A physical system boundary can sit under one actor's control while another actor carries the visible utility or compliance burden.
operational_basis: Schedules, docks, charging, tenant behavior or process decisions may be controlled by someone other than the capital provider.
financial_mechanism: Savings or compliance value may leak across contractual and metering boundaries.
typical_false_assumption: The party funding improvement automatically controls and captures the dominant variable.
hypothesis: Tenant or operator boundary ambiguity may make owner-capturable value claims inadmissible until control and capture are bounded.
rival_hypotheses: the same actor controls and captures the dominant variable
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: responsibility and control remain misaligned after review
falsification_conditions: single actor controls and captures the variable
lease and meter map fully align
allowed_claim_language: The tenant or operator boundary must be resolved before owner-capture or clean peer logic is admissible.
prohibited_claim_language: The owner will capture the value.
stop_conditions: control and capture boundary are bounded enough to rank owner-side admissibility
escalation_conditions: operator or owner confirmation required when public evidence remains insufficient
claim_permissions_impact: block peer-superiority framing when boundary drives comparability
example_outputs: If the operator controls the driver while another party pays, value may leak before it reaches the balance sheet.
tests: leased or operator-driven assets should admit this when boundary evidence is unresolved
pattern must remain bounded at L2
